messages:
ash: heads up — NimbleForms reported a spike of 504s on hosted inference for the last 30m. p99 tail jumped to ~12s, p95 ~3.5s. Customer is hitting timeouts from their side and opened a support ticket.

maria: saw the same in dashboards. gateway error rate up, and gateway logs show repeated \"request_queue_depth==1000\" on several gateway pods (we're at the configured limit). continuous-batcher backlog length is climbing to 2000+ entries.

kai: confirmed. stack traces/metrics attached in the dashboard: batcher processing rate didn't keep up with ingress; long-running KV cache spinups correlated with large seq-len requests from that tenant.

oliver-support: customer sent a small repro: a batch of 500 parallel requests with long prompts (~1k tokens). They say it used to be fine at lower throughput. They started noticing it after a retrain week.

ash: quick repro I ran: 
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" -X POST https://api.redwood-hosted/v1/generate -d '{"model":"open-likely-200b","input":"<~1k token prompt>","max_tokens":512}' & (repeat 500 times)
Gateway queue depth climbs, then 504s.

maria: mitigation steps taken so far:
- increased ingress queue depth from 1000 -> 1500 on the affected region pool (temporary)
- toggled continuous batching to strict short-timeout mode for that pool (batch_timeout 20ms -> 5ms)
Result: immediate drop in 5xx from ~8% -> ~1.2%, p99 dropped to ~4.5s. Not fully resolved.

kai: pointer: the continuous-batcher has an amortized scheduling bug when backlog > ~1.2k where it prioritizes older KV-less requests but misses high-latency already-started KV builds — leads to head-of-line stalls. I have a local repro to demonstrate scheduling inversion.

oncall-bot: incident severity elevated to P2. Paging eng-runtime and eng-infra oncall.

jess-cust-liaison: updated NimbleForms support ticket w/ temporary workaround (throttle from their side, small-burst retry jitter). They're OK with temporary throttle but want ETA for permanent fix.

oliver-support: customer reports some 502s still after the temporary change — likely from upstream model variant fallbacks hitting cold starts and further queuing.

ash: short-term playbook I propose:
- keep queue depth bumped to 1500 for 2 hours, watch memory.
- set per-tenant max_concurrent_requests to 250 for NimbleForms (they were at 600).
- deploy scheduler patch (kai) that prevents starvation when backlog > 1k (hotfix candidate).

kai: patch ready, small behavioral change to batcher scheduler; I'll run canary on one pool now. Logs show fewer preemption events in canary. Canary metrics: 5xx -> 0.6%, p99 -> 2.1s.

maria: if canary holds for 30m, roll to remaining pools in region. Also will schedule a config change to restore batch_timeout to sane value after patch.

ash: follow-ups / action items:
- kai: canary deploy + rollout if stable (ETA 30m)
- maria: keep queue depth at 1500 and monitor heap/GPU memory, revert after stable
- oliver: update customer with expected timeline and suggested short-term client retry/backoff config (jittered exponential, max attempts 4)
- jess: confirm customer is willing to cap concurrency; record in ticket

kai: canary started at 5177777815, first 10m look good. scheduling inversion counters dropped 92%.

maria: added dashboard panel showing backlog-size vs scheduler-preempt-count; will alert at backlog > 1200 next time.

oliver-support: noted in ticket: apply client-side retry with header X-Client-Retry: 1 to help tracing.

ash: long-term follow-ups (post-incident):
- add target smoothing for continuous-batcher when backlog spikes (avoid large scheduling oscillations)
- autoscale ingress queue limit intelligently per-tenant during transient spikes instead of global bump
- add tenant-level concurrency guards and clearer quota docs for customers with long sequence workloads

maria: marking incident as monitoring. will update when rollout completes or if canary regresses.

ash: thanks all. good catch on the scheduler inversion; kai great job on fast patch.

kai: will open PR and link to this thread.

oncall-bot: incident status changed to MONITORING."
